question: A solid sphere of radius 7 cm is melted and recast into smaller spheres of radius 1 cm. How many such small spheres will be formed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Number of spheres = (R/r)³

⇒ = (7/1)³

⇒ = 343

**∴ Answer = 343**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of big sphere = 7 cm

Radius of small sphere = 1 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of sphere = 4 ÷ 3 × π × r³

 R = 7 r = 1 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Volume of big sphere = 4 ÷ 3 π (7)³

⇒ Volume of one small sphere = 4 ÷ 3 π (1)³

⇒ Number of small spheres = (Volume of big sphere) ÷ (Volume of small sphere)

⇒ = [4 ÷ 3 π (7)³] ÷ [4 ÷ 3 π (1)³]

⇒ = (7)³ = 343

**∴ Final Answer = 343**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Volume Ratio:** Number of solids = (R/r)³

**Sphere Volume:** 4/3 π r³

**Concept:** Volume remains constant during melting

**Exam Tip:** Directly use cube of radius ratio
